incident-bot: [INCIDENT] High error rate + increased latency observed for Redwood hosted-api (us-west-2). Auto-pager: maya. Incident ID: INC-20260315-42. Link: <https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-20260315-42>

maya (oncall): ack — paging in. Traces look noisy, spike at 12:00 UTC. I’m attaching an initial flamegraph to the incident console.

tess (ic): I’m taking IC. Drafting status page initial update below — please review quickly. Need to publish within next 5m.

jordan (comms): :eyes: paste draft here and I’ll sweep for customer-facing wording. Keep it short.

tess (ic): INITIAL DRAFT (do not publish yet):
```json
{
  "status": "investigating",
  "components": ["Hosted API - us-west-2"],
  "impact": "Customers in us-west-2 may experience increased latency and a small percentage of failed requests.",
  "started_at": "2026-03-15T12:00:00Z",
  "update": "Our team is investigating elevated latency and error rates. We are actively scaling serving capacity and investigating autoscaler behavior. We will provide updates every 15 minutes or as new info becomes available.",
  "contact": "support@redwood.ai | https://status.redwood.ai/contact"
}
```

jordan (comms): Language tweaks: replace 'small percentage' with 'a subset of requests (~<10%)' and add recommended customer workaround: 'Please retry with exponential backoff or route to a different region if possible.' Also remove internal jargon (autoscaler) from public note.

tess (ic): updated draft with jordan's edits:
```json
{
  "status": "investigating",
  "components": ["Hosted API - us-west-2"],
  "impact": "A subset of requests (~<10%) in us-west-2 may fail or experience delays up to ~30s.",
  "started_at": "2026-03-15T12:00:00Z",
  "update": "We are investigating elevated latency and increased error rates for the Hosted API in us-west-2. Our engineers are scaling capacity and applying mitigations. Recommended workaround: retry with exponential backoff or route requests to another region.",
  "contact": "support@redwood.ai | https://status.redwood.ai/contact"
}
```

sam (legal): quick flag — ok to publish. No regulatory disclosure required at this time.

tess (ic): publishing now. Command:
```bash
curl -X POST https://status.redwood.ai/api/incidents \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"status":"investigating","components":["Hosted API - us-west-2"],"impact":"A subset of requests (~<10%) in us-west-2 may fail or experience delays up to ~30s.","started_at":"2026-03-15T12:00:00Z","update":"We are investigating elevated latency and increased error rates. Engineers are scaling capacity and applying mitigations. Recommended workaround: retry with exponential backoff or route requests to another region.","contact":"support@redwood.ai"}'
```

incident-bot: Status page update published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260315-42 (Initial) :loud_sound:

oli (sre): mitigation in progress — draining old inference nodes and bringing up additional worker pools. KV-cache warmup ongoing; that should reduce tail latency once warmed. No data loss.

maya (oncall): instrumenting more detailed traces, enabling 2x logging for affected service. Will watch for error-rate delta.

--- 15 minutes later ---

tess (ic): PERIODIC UPDATE (12:15 UTC):
- Error rate peaked at ~8% at 12:02 UTC. After scaling actions, error rate down to ~2% (12:10 UTC).
- Tail latency reduced but some long-sequence requests still see 10-20s delays.
- Impact scope: limited to Hosted API in us-west-2; Dedicated customers on pinned capacity not impacted.
- Next update in 15m or earlier if we make progress.

jordan (comms): copying update to status page. Suggest we add "no action required for most customers" line. Also drafting targeted customer email for those with SLO alerts — will post snippet in 5.

tess (ic): publishing update now.
incident-bot: Status page update published (12:15 UTC) — https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260315-42

jordan (comms): CUSTOMER EMAIL DRAFT (targeted to customers with errors/SLO alerts):
"Hi <Customer>,

We're reaching out about intermittent failures and elevated latency you may have seen on the Redwood Hosted API in us-west-2 starting at 12:00 UTC today. Our engineers have applied mitigations and error rates have decreased. Recommended short-term workaround: retry requests with exponential backoff or route to another region if traffic is multi-region. We will follow up when the incident is fully resolved. If you need immediate assistance, please reply to this email or open a support ticket at https://support.redwood.ai.

— Redwood Support"

sam (legal): ok to send to customers. Keep log links out of the customer email.

--- 20 minutes later ---

oli (sre): KV-cache warmed, additional nodes in steady state. Error rate holding at ~0.5%. Rolling restart of the autoscaling controller config reverted to last stable.

maya (oncall): monitoring — looks stable for 10min.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident INC-20260315-42 resolved at 12:35 UTC. Root cause: temporary regression in autoscaler decisioning combined with cold KV-cache behavior during rapid scaling. Mitigation: reverted autoscaler config, scaled up dedicated pool, warmed caches. Postmortem assigned to oli.

tess (ic): publishing resolved notice to status page now. Resolved message: "Incident resolved. Services are stable. Root cause identified and mitigations applied. A post-incident report will follow."

incident-bot: Resolved notice published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260315-42 — will send automated subscriber emails.

jordan (comms): I’ll send the customer-targeted email and update the incident summary for the support site.

tess (ic): thanks team. Closing the on-call handoff: maya -> oli for postmortem. Checklist:
- oli to own postmortem (draft due 24h)
- ops to confirm no regression in 48h
- comms to send follow-up to subscribers

maya (oncall): ack handoff, available to help with logs.

oli (sre): will have draft postmortem by 12:30 UTC tomorrow.

jordan (comms): :thumbsup: good job everyone.
